reconcile.connective: The strongest way to keep both numbers standing reads the 42 as a co-regency date — Ahaziah crowned during his father's reign, then confirmed in his own right.

discrepancy.connective: Several harmonizing commentators themselves concede the figures cannot both stand; Adam Clarke calls it a manifest contradiction, an objection Steve Wells presses verbatim at the Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "How old was Ahaziah when he began to reign?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: It is most evident that, if we follow the reading in Chronicles, it makes the son two years older than his own father! for his father began to reign when he was thirty-two years old, and reigned eight years, and so died, being forty years old… After all, here is a most manifest contradiction, that cannot be removed but by having recourse to violent modes of solution.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: A harmonizing commentator conceding the discrepancy: the 42 reading makes the son older than the father, and Clarke flatly calls it a manifest contradiction removable only by violent solutions. Rare verbatim concession -> filled discrepancy pole (id-255 pattern). Two non-adjacent spans joined sense-preservingly; first truncated mid-sentence with the ellipsis marker, second ends on a real source period.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Ahaziah might have been twenty-two years old, according to Kg2 8:26 … but he could not have been forty-two, as stated here, without being two years older than his own father!… Both readings cannot be true; is that therefore likely to be genuine that makes the son two years older than the father who begat him?
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke's parallel note at the Chronicles end states the same concession from the other side: both readings cannot be true. Reinforces the filled discrepancy pole; same distinct conceding voice keyed to the second cited verse. Three verbatim spans joined sense-preservingly: an ellipsis drops only the editorial parenthetical '(note),' between the first two clauses; a second ellipsis skips the off-tension Syriac/Septuagint and Hebrew-letter exposition to reach 'Both readings cannot be true'. Ends on a source question mark; no fabricated period.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Which is to be understood, that he was made king when his father reigned, but after his father's death he was confirmed king when he was forty-two years old, as 2 Chron. 22:2.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The single strongest harmonization that lets both numbers stand: the co-regency reading -- 22 at the first accession during his father's reign, 42 (read as a family/dynasty date) at his confirmation afterward. Full sentence ending on a real source period; parity-capped to one reconcile excerpt on this discrepancy_first row.

pd_work.note: Gill canvasses the chief harmonizations of the 22-vs-42 figure (co-regency, mother's/dynasty age) and judges it best to acknowledge a copyist's confusion of the numeral letters, noting the Syriac and some Septuagint copies read twenty-two.
